findings.what: feed_info.txt has no technical contact (feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url).
findings.why: Trip-planning apps and regional data coordinators have nobody to email when they spot a problem with your feed, so problems linger.

completeness.name: completeness
completeness.summary: 100% of stops state wheelchair accessibility (1% marked accessible, 99% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a stop is physically usable. Fare data is published.

findings.effort: Usually an export-tool fix, not hand editing.
findings.fix: Check the flagged stops' shape_dist_traveled against the route shape, and re-generate it on export if they disagree.
findings.what: Some stops sit far from the route line, going by the feed's own distance values.
findings.why: Trip planners may draw the route down the wrong streets or point riders to the wrong corner.

findings.effort: One setting in most export tools.
findings.fix: Remove past service periods the next time you export the feed.
findings.what: Some service calendars in the feed have already ended.
findings.why: Expired calendars are dead weight and can hide real schedule problems from your staff and vendors.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'same_name_and_description_for_stop' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Same name and description for stop (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: Usually a re-export from your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Export and publish an updated GTFS feed that covers at least the next 30 days of service.
findings.what: This feed's service calendar runs out within the next 7 days.
findings.why: When the calendar ends, Google Maps and other trip planners drop your agency entirely. Riders see no service at all.

findings.effort: One field, set once in export settings.
findings.fix: Add feed_contact_email or feed_contact_url to feed_info.txt.
findings.what: feed_info.txt lists no contact email and no contact URL.
findings.why: Without a contact, apps like Google Maps can't reach you when they find a problem in the feed.

findings.effort: A field at a time; not urgent.
findings.fix: Review the flagged fields and fill in the ones your riders would use.
findings.what: Some files leave out fields that GTFS asks for but does not require.
findings.why: Recommended fields like agency_phone or stop descriptions make the feed more useful to riders and trip planners.

findings.effort: One setting in most export tools.
findings.fix: Trim past service periods the next time you export.
findings.what: Many of the feed's trips don't run at all in the next 7 days.
findings.why: It usually means old service periods are still in the export, making the feed bigger and harder to check.

findings.effort: Usually a bulk edit in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Set trip_headsign to the trip's last stop or its overall destination.
findings.what: Some trip headsigns name a stop along the way, not the final destination.
findings.why: The sign should tell riders where the bus ends up, so a midpoint name can send them the wrong way.

correctness.name: correctness
correctness.summary: The MobilityData validator flagged 8 kinds of issue across 70 instances (0 error, 57 warning, 13 informational).

findings.effort: Usually one export setting; export on a schedule so it never lapses again.

findings.why: When the calendar runs out, trip planners stop showing this agency even though the buses are still running. Riders are told the service does not exist.

ntd_id_alignment.detail: Your feed's agency_id is lavta-ca-us; your National Transit Database ID is 90144. A feed that serves several agencies (a shared regional feed) can legitimately carry more than one agency_id. The values do not need to equal the five-digit NTD ID, so this difference is allowed and carries no score.
ntd_id_alignment.fix: Confirm that P-50 crosswalks agency_id lavta-ca-us to NTD ID 90144, and keep the feed value stable. Do not change it solely to make the two values equal.

pillars.detail: Service data expired 97 days ago, so FTA would find the link out of date.
agency.txt provides agency_id. For RY2026, keep one stable value for each NTD reporter represented in the feed and crosswalk each value on the P-50 form.

ntd_readiness.summary: Resolve this before you certify on the D-10. Service data expired 97 days ago, so FTA would find the link out of date.

recommendations.effort: A per-route color setting in your scheduling software.
recommendations.fix: Adjust route_color or route_text_color so each pair clears 4.5:1. Often switching the text between black and white is enough.
recommendations.what: 23 route badge(s) pair a color and text color below the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast bar (10R, 18, 2, 201, 20X, and more).
recommendations.why: Low-contrast route badges are hard to read for riders with low vision and wash out on a phone screen in sunlight at the stop.

recommendations.effort: A short text field per affected stop; start with the busiest.
recommendations.fix: Add tts_stop_name with the spoken form, e.g. 'Main Street and Second Avenue', for the affected stops.
recommendations.what: 655 stop name(s) use abbreviations or symbols a screen reader may mispronounce, with no spoken form set ("Springtown Blvd & Bluebell Dr", "Dalton Ave & N Vasco Rd", "Junction Ave & Chestnut St WB", and more).
recommendations.why: Riders who use a screen reader hear the raw name, so 'Main St & 2nd Ave' can come out as 'Main saint' or drop the ampersand.
